sections.skill: Agree on partner roles, ownership and disagreements before starting

questions.prompt: Which topic should partners agree on in writing?

choices.text: Which music plays in the office

questions.correct_answer: How ties are broken
questions.intro: Starting with a PARTNER can add skills, money and support, but disagreements are a common reason partnerships fail. Before starting, agree in writing on: each person's ROLE and time commitment, ownership percentages and money contributed, how decisions are made (and how ties are broken), how profits are shared, what happens if someone wants to leave or stops contributing, and how to resolve disagreements. Talk openly about goals, risk tolerance and money. Friendship is not a substitute for a written agreement.

sections.skill: Planning a road trip with a friend

questions.prompt: Who drives when is like what?
questions.correct_answer: Each partner's role
questions.intro: Before a long road trip, friends decide who drives when, how gas money is split, and what happens if one wants to stop early. Without that talk, small annoyances grow into big fights by day three. A business partnership is a much longer trip with more money at stake, so the same planning matters even more.
